Vadakkan culture

Vadakkan means "northern". Perambra sits in northern Malabar, a land known for warriors, ritual art and ballads. Our cafe is a small part of that story.

Kalaripayattu

Kerala's ancient martial art was practised in training halls called kalaris across Malabar. It joins quick footwork, sword and shield, and a deep respect for the teacher.

Many northern families grew up around the kalari, and the hearty, filling food of the region was made for people who worked and trained hard.

Theyyam

Every winter, northern Kerala's temples and village shrines host Theyyam, a ritual art where performers in towering headdresses, bright face paint and red costumes embody gods and heroes.

It is one of the most vivid sights in Kerala and a reason to visit the north.

Vadakkan Pattukal

The Vadakkan Pattukal are the ballads of northern Malabar, sung for generations. They tell of brave heroes such as Thacholi Othenan and the fearless Unniyarcha, of family feuds, honour and kalari duels.

Many of these tales belong to the Vatakara and Kozhikode region, close to where we serve you today.

Mundu & kasavu

The off-white mundu with a gold kasavu border is Kerala's most loved cloth, worn at festivals, weddings and temple visits. Its gold edge inspires the borders on this website.

The Malabar table

Malabar cooking is known for flaky porotta, coconut-rich curries, mappas, neypathal and strong tea. It is food built for sharing and for slow conversation.

At Vadakkan Cafe we carry those flavours forward, one plate and one chai at a time.

Come hungry. Leave with a story.
